From a safe floating spawn island, the player sees a bright ascending route, three numbered checkpoint beacons, a visibly moving platform over a warned open-sky hazard, and a finish arch in the distance. The opening jumps teach the course’s comfortable spacing before Checkpoint 1; the middle section introduces the moving-platform crossing and Checkpoint 2; a short final stair-and-gap sequence reaches Checkpoint 3 and the finish. Each valid checkpoint activates only in order, visibly changes state, and plays synchronized Marketplace confirmation audio. Early contact with later checkpoints does nothing and cannot advance progress. Falling into the marked hazard or below the course returns the character to the last valid checkpoint without resetting checkpoint count or elapsed time. A persistent, legible HUD shows checkpoint progress and live elapsed time on desktop and touch. Finishing freezes the result, presents completion time, and exposes a deliberate Replay button; replay explicitly starts a fresh run at spawn rather than restarting automatically.

Marketplace discovery and source inspection precede implementation decisions for checkpoint, moving-platform, and short-course components. Existing useful geometry, scripts, motion, activation feedback, animation, and embedded media must be preserved when compatible. Exact integration-script ownership remains undecided for discovery-dependent systems until their hierarchies, interfaces, dependencies, and source safety are inspected. The course remains intentionally small: no multiplayer systems, persistence, purchases, combat, upgrades, or sprawling side areas. The moving crossing should have a strong horizontal silhouette, visible endpoints, and contrasting motion-path markers so players can judge timing before jumping.

The fall zone is open sky beneath and between islands, made unmistakable with warm red-orange warning stripes, hazard signs, and edge lights at committed crossings without cluttering safe jump edges. Use atmospheric sky depth and restrained cloud forms to make height apparent while maintaining high contrast around walkable surfaces. The spawn island, each checkpoint, moving-platform crossing, and finish arch form distinct landmarks along one forward route; no decorative branch should imply an alternate path or shortcut.

Keep geometry readable and forgiving: broad landing pads, comfortable standard-character jumps, sufficient headroom, non-slippery surfaces, and a safe checkpoint return orientation facing the next obstacle. The finish should be a larger arch or gate with a clear celebratory color change after completion. HUD hierarchy is minimal: checkpoint status is the primary label, elapsed time is secondary, and the completion card is centered with a large touch-safe Replay button. UI must respect screen insets, remain readable at common desktop and phone resolutions, and not cover movement controls.
